- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 5–10% for the immediate follow-up period.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), check sentiment for bullish bias — if present, consider mean reversion in next 7–10 days.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., <5% under for 3+ days), sentiment may be bearish — consider upward adjustment if sentiment turns neutral or positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >5% avg. daily gain), model often lags — adjust forecast to reflect momentum, especially if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast with sentiment’s recent trend, not just historical mean.
